text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.95% today after two days of sharp gains that pushed the stock up nearly 5% from Monday's close. The decline came as oil prices retreated: U.S. crude dropped to $96.24 per barrel today after climbing on Middle East supply concerns the previous two days. While refineries are running hot at 92.7% capacity and global crude sits at $125.44 per barrel—a premium that typically favors U.S. refiners' margins—the pullback in prices suggests some of yesterday's geopolitical risk premium evaporated as traders assessed the actual fallout from escalating Iranian attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

The stock's two-week surge of 13% reflects the broader volatility energy markets have faced: escalating Middle East tensions initially lifted crude prices sharply, helping refiners' profitability, but today's retreat shows those gains aren't stable as long as the outcome of shipping disruptions remains uncertain. With diesel and gasoline inventories relatively tight (105 and 205 million barrels respectively), any sustained supply disruption would matter more to refining margins than a one-day pullback in crude prices.
